content.title: About
content.content: Tomatoes, crushed, canned are a ready‑to‑use product made from ripe tomatoes that have been peeled, seeded, finely ground into a smooth puree and sealed in airtight glass or metal cans. The product retains the characteristic tomato flavor, aroma and bright red color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes were first domesticated in Central and South America more than 5,000 years ago.
Canning preserves over 90 % of the tomato’s vitamin C and lycopene.
Lycopene from processed tomatoes is more bioavailable than from fresh fruit.
Canned crushed tomatoes are a staple in many cuisines: Italian pasta sauces, Mexican salsa, Indian chutney.
Cans are typically sterilized at 115 °C for 30‑45 minutes, ensuring a long shelf life.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tomatoes contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some canned varieties contain added salt; those with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Bisphenol‑A in packaging
items.content: Metal cans may be coated with epoxy resins that contain BPA; opt for glass jars if this is a concern.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Crushed canned tomatoes are ideal for sauces, soups, stews, pizza, and rice‑based dishes. Add them directly to hot dishes or briefly heat with a splash of olive oil and seasonings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the product refrigerated and use within 3‑5 days. Discard if you notice mold, off‑odor, or any signs of spoilage.
